name: HZ2 field (Hubble)
blurb: A deep field toward the distant galaxy HZ2, seen by Hubble.
label: hz2-hubble
story: Somewhere in this deep frame is HZ2, an ordinary star-forming galaxy seen a billion years after the Big Bang that also shines as a Lyman-alpha emitter. Hubble mapped its starlight to compare with ALMA's view of its gas and dust.

claims.text: HZ2 is a galaxy in a sample of normal galaxies at 5<z<6 targeted by Hubble program 13641
HZ2 lies in the COSMOS field
These galaxies are seen a billion years after the Big Bang
Hubble mapped the galaxies' starlight to compare with ALMA measurements of their gas and dust
HZ2 meets the selection criteria for a Lyman-alpha emitter
